mishnayos.summary: For three days before a non-Jewish holiday for their idols, we may not do business with them. We don't want them to be happy and thank their idol on their holiday.

chunks.he: לִפְנֵי אֵידֵיהֶן שֶׁל גּוֹיִם שְׁלשָׁה יָמִים
chunks.en: For three days before the holidays of non-Jews,
chunks.st: On the three days before the festivals of gentiles
chunks.stMore: the following actions are prohibited, as they would bring joy to the gentile, who would subsequently give thanks to his object of idol worship on his festival:

words.note: Holidays they make for their idols.

chunks.en: it is forbidden to do business with them,
chunks.st: It is prohibited to engage in business with them;

words.note: Taking and giving means doing business.

chunks.en: to lend them things, or to borrow things from them,
chunks.st: to lend items to them or to borrow items from them;

chunks.en: to lend them money, or to borrow money from them,
chunks.st: to lend money to them or to borrow money from them;

chunks.en: to pay them what we owe, or to collect what they owe us.
chunks.st: and to repay debts owed to them or to collect repayment of debts from them.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.he: נִפְרָעִין מֵהֶן מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מֵצֵר לוֹ.
chunks.en: We may collect what they owe us, because paying back makes him sad.
chunks.st: One may collect repayment of debts from them because this causes the gentile distress.

chunks.en: The Rabbis said to him,
chunks.st: The Rabbis said to Rabbi Yehuda:

chunks.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמֵּצֵר הוּא עַכְשָׁיו,
chunks.en: Even though he is sad now,
chunks.st: Even though he is distressed now,

chunks.en: he is happy later on.
chunks.explain: He is glad the debt is gone, and may thank his idol.
chunks.st: when he repays the money, he is happy afterward
chunks.stMore: that he is relieved of the debt, and therefore there is concern that he will give thanks to his object of idol worship on his festival.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yishmael says the days after their holidays are forbidden too. The Sages say only the days before are forbidden.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yishmael says:

chunks.he: שְׁלשָׁה יָמִים לִפְנֵיהֶם וּשְׁלשָׁה יָמִים לְאַחֲרֵיהֶם,
chunks.en: three days before their holidays and three days after them
chunks.st: On the three days before the festivals of gentiles and on the three days after them,

chunks.en: it is forbidden.
chunks.st: it is prohibited to engage in business with those gentiles.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: before their holidays it is forbidden,
chunks.st: It is prohibited to engage in business with them before their festivals,

chunks.en: after their holidays it is allowed.
chunks.st: but it is permitted to engage in business with them after their festivals.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah lists the holidays of the non-Jews, like the king's birthday. Private celebrations of one person are forbidden only on that day and only with that man.

chunks.en: These are the holidays of the non-Jews:
chunks.st: And these are the festivals of gentiles:

chunks.en: Kalenda, and Saturnalia,
chunks.st: Kalenda, Saturnalia,

words.note: A Roman winter holiday.
Another Roman winter holiday.

chunks.en: and Kratesis, and the holiday of their kings,
chunks.st: and Kratesis, and the day of the festival of their kings,

words.note: A day honoring the king.

chunks.en: and the king's birthday,
chunks.st: and the birthday of the king,

chunks.en: and the day the king died.
chunks.st: and the anniversary of the day of the death of the king.

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: Any death where they burn things in public,
chunks.st: Every death that includes public burning

chunks.en: has avodah zarah in it — it is a holiday for idols.
chunks.st: is a festival that includes idol worship,

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: And one where they don't burn things,
chunks.st: and any death that does not include public burning

chunks.en: has no avodah zarah in it.
chunks.st: is not a festival that includes idol worship.

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: The day a non-Jew shaves his beard and his long hair,
chunks.st: But in the case of the day of shaving his, i.e., a gentile’s, beard and his locks,

chunks.en: the day he came back from the sea,
chunks.st: and the day of his ascent from the sea,

chunks.en: and the day he came out of prison,
chunks.st: and the day that he left prison,

words.note: Prison.

chunks.en: and a non-Jew who made a feast for his son,
chunks.st: and also in the case of a gentile who prepared a wedding feast for his son

chunks.en: it is forbidden only on that
chunks.st: and celebrates on that day, engaging in business is prohibited only on that

chunks.en: day, and only with that man.
chunks.st: day and with that man.

mishnayos.summary: If a city is having an idol holiday, may we do business outside it, or travel there? It depends on the place and the road.

chunks.en: A city that has avodah zarah,
chunks.explain: It is having a holiday for its idol.
chunks.st: In the case of a city in which there is active idol worship,

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: outside it, it is allowed to do business.
chunks.st: it is permitted to engage in business transactions with gentiles who live outside of the city.

chunks.en: If the avodah zarah was outside the city,
chunks.st: If the idol worship is outside the city,

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: inside the city it is allowed.
chunks.st: it is permitted to engage in business within the city.

chunks.en: What about going there?
chunks.st: What is the halakha with regard to traveling there,
chunks.stMore: a place where a pagan festival is being celebrated?

chunks.en: When the road goes only to that place,
chunks.st: When the road is designated only for that place,

chunks.en: it is forbidden. But if he could walk
chunks.explain: People would think he is going to the idol's holiday.
chunks.st: it is prohibited to use the road,
chunks.stMore: as onlookers will assume that the traveler intends to join the festival.

chunks.en: on it to another place,
chunks.st: But if one were able to travel on it to arrive at another place,

chunks.he: מֻתָּר. עִיר שֶׁיֶּשׁ בָּהּ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְהָיוּ
chunks.en: it is allowed. A city that has avodah zarah, and there were
chunks.st: it is permitted to use the road
chunks.stMore: to reach the place that is observing the festival.

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: stores in it — some decorated, and some not decorated,
chunks.explain: Decorated stores paid money to the idol.
chunks.st: With regard to a city in which idol worship is practiced and in which there are stores that are adorned for the sake of idol worship and there are others that are not adorned,

chunks.en: this really happened in Beis She'an,
chunks.st: this was in fact an incident that occurred in Beit She’an,

words.note: Beis She'an is a city in Eretz Yisrael.

chunks.en: and the Sages said,
chunks.st: and the Sages said:

chunks.en: the decorated stores are forbidden, and the ones not decorated are allowed.
chunks.st: With regard to the adorned shops, it is prohibited to buy from them, but in the case of those that are not adorned it is permitted.

mishnayos.summary: Some things are used only for idol worship, so we may not sell them to non-Jews. Other things we may sell, unless the buyer says he wants them for his idol.

chunks.en: These things are forbidden to sell to non-Jews:
chunks.st: These are the items that it is prohibited to sell to a gentile
chunks.stMore: at any time of year, as they are used specifically for idol worship:

chunks.en: itzterubalin, and benos shuach and their stems,
chunks.st: Itzterubalin, benot shuaḥ, petotarot,

words.note: A kind of fruit.
Benos shuach are a kind of white figs.

chunks.en: and frankincense, and a white rooster.
chunks.st: frankincense, and a white rooster.

words.note: A sweet-smelling spice they burned for idols.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: it is allowed to sell him a white rooster
chunks.st: It is permitted to sell a white rooster

chunks.en: together with other roosters.
chunks.st: to a gentile provided that it is sold along with other types of roosters.

chunks.en: But when it is sold by itself,
chunks.st: But when it is sold by itself,

chunks.en: he cuts off its toe and sells it to him,
chunks.st: one should cut off its toe and sell it to the gentile,

chunks.he: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין מַקְרִיבִין חָסֵר לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.
chunks.en: because they don't bring a damaged animal to their idol.
chunks.st: because they do not sacrifice a defective animal to their object of idol worship.

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: And all other things,
chunks.st: And with regard to all remaining items,

chunks.en: if he says nothing, it is allowed,
chunks.st: without specification it is permitted to sell them,

chunks.en: but if he says they are for his idol, it is forbidden.
chunks.st: but with specification it is prohibited to sell them.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: even a good palm tree, and chatzav,
chunks.st: Even in the case of a good palm tree, ḥatzav,

words.note: A kind of plant.

chunks.en: and naklav, are forbidden to sell to non-Jews.
chunks.st: and naklav, it is prohibited to sell them to gentiles.

words.note: Another kind of plant.

mishnayos.summary: May we sell animals to non-Jews? Small animals depend on the local custom. Big animals that do work are never sold, so a Jew's animal won't work on Shabbos.

chunks.he: מְקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ לִמְכֹּר בְּהֵמָה דַקָּה לְגוֹיִם,
chunks.en: In a place where people sold small animals to non-Jews,
chunks.st: In a place where the residents were accustomed to sell small domesticated animals to gentiles,

chunks.en: we may sell. In a place where they did not sell,
chunks.st: one may sell them. In a place where they were not accustomed to sell them,

chunks.en: we may not sell.
chunks.st: one may not sell them.

chunks.en: And in every place, we may not sell
chunks.st: But in every place, one may not sell

chunks.en: them big animals,
chunks.st: them large livestock,

chunks.en: calves or young horses,
chunks.st: calves, or foals,

chunks.en: whether whole or hurt.
chunks.explain: We don't want a Jew's animal to do work on Shabbos.
chunks.st: whether these animals are whole or damaged.
chunks.stMore: The Sages prohibited these sales lest a Jew’s animal perform labor for the gentile on Shabbat in violation of an explicit Torah prohibition, as explained in the Gemara.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah allows a hurt animal.
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda permits the sale of a damaged animal
chunks.stMore: because it is incapable of performing labor,

chunks.en: And Ben Beseira allows a horse.
chunks.st: and ben Beteira permits the sale of a horse
chunks.stMore: for riding, because riding a horse on Shabbat is not prohibited by Torah law.

mishnayos.summary: We may not sell non-Jews dangerous animals, or help them build places used to hurt people. We may help build a bathhouse, but not the spot where they put an idol.

chunks.he: אֵין מוֹכְרִין לָהֶם דֻּבִּין וַאֲרָיוֹת וְכָל
chunks.en: We may not sell them bears, or lions, or any
chunks.st: One may not sell bears, or lions, or any item

chunks.en: thing that can hurt many people.
chunks.st: that can cause injury to the public, to gentiles.

chunks.en: We may not build with them a basilica,
chunks.st: One may not build with them a basilica [basileki],

words.note: A big building where judges sat.

chunks.en: a courthouse, or a stadium,
chunks.st: a tribunal [gardom], a stadium [itztadeyya],

words.note: Where they judged people to be killed.
A big field where people were hurt for a show.

chunks.he: וּבִימָה. אֲבָל בּוֹנִים עִמָּהֶם בִּימוֹסְיָאוֹת וּבֵית מֶרְחֲצָאוֹת.
chunks.en: or a tall platform. But we may build with them small platforms and bathhouses.
chunks.st: or a platform. But one may build with them small platforms [bimmusiot] and bathhouses.

chunks.he: הִגִּיעוּ לַכִּפָּה שֶׁמַּעֲמִידִין בָּהּ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
chunks.en: Once they reach the dome where they put up their avodah zarah,
chunks.st: Even in this case, once he reaches the arched chamber in the bath where the gentiles put up objects of idol worship,

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: it is forbidden to build.
chunks.st: it is prohibited to build it.

mishnayos.summary: We may not make jewelry for idols. We may not sell non-Jews things attached to the ground in Eretz Yisrael. Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yosei argue about renting and selling houses and fields in different places.

chunks.en: We may not make jewelry for avodah zarah,
chunks.st: And one may not fashion jewelry for an object of idol worship,

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: like necklaces, nose rings and rings.
chunks.st: and this applies to jewelry such as necklaces [katla’ot], nose rings, and rings.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: if it is for pay, it is allowed.
chunks.st: If one fashions them in exchange for payment, it is permitted.
chunks.stMore: The mishna returns to the issue of selling items to gentiles:

chunks.en: We may not sell them something attached to the ground,
chunks.st: One may not sell to a gentile any item that is attached to the ground,

chunks.en: but he may sell it once it is cut off.
chunks.st: but one may sell such an item once it is severed from the ground.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.he: מוֹכֵר הוּא לוֹ עַל מְנָת לָקוֹץ.
chunks.en: he may sell it to him if it will be cut off.
chunks.st: It is not necessary to sever the item from the ground; rather, one may sell it on the condition that it be severed.

chunks.he: אֵין מַשְׂכִּירִין לָהֶם בָּתִּים בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
chunks.en: We may not rent houses to them in Eretz Yisrael,
chunks.st: One may not rent a house to a gentile in Eretz Yisrael,

chunks.en: and of course not fields.
chunks.st: and needless to say one may not rent fields to them, as explained in the Gemara.

chunks.en: And in Syria we may rent houses to them,
chunks.st: And in Syria one may rent houses to gentiles,

words.note: A land next to Eretz Yisrael.

chunks.en: but not fields.
chunks.st: but one may not rent fields.

chunks.en: And outside Eretz Yisrael we may sell them
chunks.st: And outside of Eretz Yisrael

chunks.en: houses and rent them fields,
chunks.st: one may sell houses and rent fields to gentiles;

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: in Eretz Yisrael we may rent houses to them,
chunks.st: In Eretz Yisrael one may rent houses to gentiles

chunks.en: but not fields.
chunks.st: but one may not rent fields.

chunks.en: And in Syria we may sell houses and rent fields.
chunks.st: And in Syria one may sell houses to them and rent fields,

chunks.en: And outside Eretz Yisrael we may sell both.
chunks.st: and outside of Eretz Yisrael one may sell both these, houses, and those, fields.

mishnayos.summary: Even where renting a house is allowed, it may not be rented for living in, because he will bring his idols into it. And a bathhouse may never be rented to a non-Jew.

chunks.en: Even in a place where they said we may rent,
chunks.st: Even in a place with regard to which the Sages said that it is permitted for a Jew to rent a house to a gentile,

chunks.en: they did not mean for a house to live in,
chunks.st: they did not say that one may rent it for use as a residence,

chunks.he: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מַכְנִיס לְתוֹכוֹ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
chunks.en: because he will bring avodah zarah into it,
chunks.st: because the gentile will bring objects of idol worship into it,

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: as it says in the Torah: "And do not
chunks.st: as it is stated:

words.note: The fifth book of the Torah.

chunks.en: bring an abomination into your house."
chunks.st: “You shall not bring an abomination into your house” (Deuteronomy 7:26),
chunks.stMore: and this is still considered the house of a Jew.

words.note: Something Hashem hates, like an idol.

chunks.en: And in every place he may not rent
chunks.st: And for the same reason, in every place,

chunks.en: him the bathhouse,
chunks.st: one may not rent a bathhouse to a gentile,

chunks.en: because it is called by his name.
chunks.explain: People will think the Jew runs it on Shabbos.
chunks.st: since it is called by the name of the owner,
chunks.stMore: and onlookers will think that the Jew is operating it on Shabbat.

mishnayos.summary: We may not leave an animal at a non-Jew's inn, and a Jew may not be alone with non-Jews who were suspected of doing bad things. The mishnah also says when a Jewish woman may help a non-Jewish woman with a baby.

chunks.he: אֵין מַעֲמִידִין בְּהֵמָה בְּפֻנְדְּקָאוֹת שֶׁל גּוֹיִם,
chunks.en: We may not leave an animal in the inns of non-Jews,
because they are suspected of treating animals in a forbidden way.
And a woman may not be alone with them,
because they are suspected of forbidden relationships.
And a person may not be alone with them,
because they are suspected of killing.

chunks.he: בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא תְיַלֵּד אֶת הַנָּכְרִית,
chunks.en: A Jewish woman may not help a non-Jewish woman give birth,
because she is helping bring a child for avodah zarah.
chunks.explain: The baby will grow up to serve idols.

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: But a non-Jewish woman may help a Jewish woman give birth.

chunks.he: בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא תָנִיק בְּנָהּ שֶׁל נָכְרִית,
chunks.en: A Jewish woman may not nurse the baby of a non-Jewish woman,

chunks.he: אֲבָל נָכְרִית מְנִיקָה בְנָהּ שֶׁל יִשְׂרְאֵלִית בִּרְשׁוּתָהּ:
chunks.en: but a non-Jewish woman may nurse a Jewish woman's baby in the Jewish woman's home.

mishnayos.summary: We may get healing from a non-Jew for our animals, but not for ourselves. Rabbi Meir and the Sages argue about getting a haircut from a non-Jew.

chunks.en: We may get healing from them for our belongings,
chunks.explain: This means healing our animals.
chunks.st: One may be treated by gentiles, provided that it is monetary treatment,

chunks.en: but not healing for our own bodies.
chunks.st: but not personal treatment.

chunks.en: And we may not get a haircut from them anywhere,
chunks.explain: We worry he might hurt him with the razor.
chunks.st: And one may not have his hair cut by them anywhere,
chunks.stMore: due to the danger that the gentile will kill him with the razor;

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: in a public place it is allowed,
chunks.st: In the public thoroughfare, it is permitted to have one’s hair cut by a gentile,

chunks.en: but not when they are alone together.
chunks.st: but not when the Jew and gentile are alone together.

mishnayos.stIntro: The mishna discusses the issue of accepting certain professional services from a gentile.

mishnayos.summary: Some things of non-Jews are so forbidden that we may not even get any use from them, like their wine. Meat going out of an idol's house is forbidden too, and we may not do business with people on their way to an idol's holiday.

chunks.en: These things of non-Jews
chunks.st: These are items that belong to gentiles

chunks.en: are forbidden, and we may not even get any use from them:
chunks.st: and are prohibited to Jews, and their prohibition is that of an item from which deriving benefit is prohibited:

words.note: We may not even get any use or money from it.

chunks.he: הַיַּיִן, וְהַחֹמֶץ שֶׁל גּוֹיִם שֶׁהָיָה מִתְּחִלָּתוֹ יַיִן,
chunks.en: their wine, and non-Jews' vinegar that started out as wine,
chunks.explain: It may have been poured out for an idol.
chunks.st: Wine, and vinegar belonging to gentiles that was originally wine,

chunks.en: and Hadrianic clay pots,
chunks.st: and Hadrianic earthenware,

words.note: Clay pieces that had wine soaked into them.

chunks.en: and animal skins with a hole cut by the heart.
chunks.explain: They cut out the heart to offer to their idol.
chunks.st: and hides with a tear opposite the heart.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: when its cut is round, it is forbidden.
chunks.st: A hide is prohibited only when the tear around its heart is circular,

chunks.en: If it is long, it is allowed.
chunks.st: but if it is elongated it is permitted,
chunks.stMore: as gentiles will sacrifice a heart only when it has been removed by a circular laceration.

chunks.en: Meat going into a house of avodah zarah
chunks.st: Meat that enters the house of idol worship

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: is allowed.
chunks.st: is permitted,

chunks.en: But meat coming out is forbidden,
chunks.st: and meat that exits this house is prohibited,

chunks.en: because it is like an offering to dead things — idols.
chunks.st: because it is considered as offerings to the dead, i.e., to idols;

words.note: Idols have no life, so they are called dead.

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Akiva says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Akiva.

chunks.en: Those going to an idol's holiday,
chunks.st: With regard to those going to a festival of idolatry [tarput],

chunks.en: it is forbidden to do business with them.
chunks.st: it is prohibited to engage in business with them.

chunks.en: And those coming back are allowed.
chunks.st: And with regard to those who are coming from it, it is permitted to engage in business with them.

mishnayos.stIntro: This mishna discusses the halakhic status of various items that belong to gentiles.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Meir and the Sages argue about some things of non-Jews: are they forbidden even to use, or only to eat?

chunks.en: Wineskins of non-Jews and their jugs,
chunks.st: Wineskins and jugs belonging to gentiles,

chunks.en: with a Jew's wine stored in them,
chunks.st: which have a Jew’s wine contained in them,

chunks.en: are forbidden, and we may not even get any use from them.
chunks.st: are prohibited to Jews, and their prohibition is that of an item from which deriving benefit is prohibited;

words.note: We may not even get any use or money from it.

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: they are not forbidden for use.
chunks.st: Their prohibition is not that of an item from which deriving benefit is prohibited.

Its stones, its wood and its dust
make tamei like a sheretz,

words.note: A small crawling animal that makes things tamei.

chunks.en: as it says in the Torah: "You shall find it disgusting."
chunks.explain: The Torah uses a word like sheretz.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,

chunks.he: כַּנִּדָּה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (ישעיה ל) תִּזְרֵם כְּמוֹ דָוָה,
chunks.en: like a niddah, as it says: "Throw them away like something tamei,

words.note: A kind of tumah.
A book of the Navi.

chunks.en: say to it: Go away!"
Just as a niddah makes tamei by carrying,
so too avodah zarah makes tamei by carrying.

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

mishnayos.summary: There are three kinds of houses, three kinds of stones, and three kinds of ashera trees: some are forbidden forever, and some become allowed. The mishnah also tells a story of Rabbi Shimon and a worshipped tree.

chunks.en: There are three kinds of houses.
chunks.st: With regard to idol worship there are three types of houses, each with its own halakhot.

chunks.en: A house built from the start for avodah zarah
chunks.st: A house that one built initially for the purpose of idol worship

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: is forbidden.
chunks.st: is forbidden,
chunks.stMore: i.e., it is prohibited to derive benefit from such a house.

chunks.en: If he plastered it and painted it for avodah zarah, and added something new,
chunks.st: If one plastered a house or cemented it for the purpose of idol worship, and he thereby added a layer to the walls of the house,

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: he takes off what he added.
chunks.st: one removes that which he added,
chunks.stMore: and the rest of the house is permitted.

chunks.en: If he brought avodah zarah into it and took it out,
chunks.st: If one brought an object of idol worship into a house temporarily and then removed it,

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: it is allowed.
chunks.st: the house is then permitted.

chunks.en: There are three kinds of stones.
chunks.st: With regard to idol worship there are three types of stones, each with its own halakhot.

chunks.en: A stone that was cut from the start for an idol's stand
chunks.st: A stone that one initially hewed for use in a platform [bimos] for an idol

chunks.en: is forbidden.
chunks.st: is forbidden.

chunks.he: סִיְּדָהּ וְכִיְּרָהּ לְשֵׁם עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְחִדֵּשׁ,
chunks.en: If he plastered it and painted it for avodah zarah, and added something new,
chunks.st: If one plastered a stone or cemented it for the sake of idol worship,

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: he takes off what he added.
chunks.st: one removes that which he plastered or cemented and the stone is permitted.

chunks.en: If he stood avodah zarah on it and removed it,
chunks.st: If one erected an object of idol worship upon a stone and subsequently removed it,

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: it is allowed.
chunks.st: the stone is then permitted.

chunks.en: There are three kinds of ashera trees.
chunks.st: There are three types of trees that were used as part of idolatrous rites [ashera]:

words.note: Trees that are worshipped as idols.

chunks.he: אִילָן שֶׁנְּטָעוֹ מִתְּחִלָּה לְשֵׁם עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
chunks.en: A tree planted from the start for avodah zarah
chunks.st: A tree that one initially planted for the sake of idol worship

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: is forbidden.
chunks.st: is forbidden,
chunks.stMore: and one may not derive benefit from any part of the tree.

chunks.he: גִּדְּעוֹ וּפִסְּלוֹ לְשֵׁם עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְהֶחֱלִיף,
chunks.en: If he cut it down or trimmed it for avodah zarah, and it grew back,
chunks.st: If one lopped off part of the trunk of a tree or trimmed its branches for the sake of idol worship, i.e., to worship that which would regrow there, and the tree’s trunk or limbs regrew,

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: he takes off what grew back.
chunks.st: one removes that which has regrown
chunks.stMore: and burn it. The remainder of the tree is then permitted.

chunks.en: If he stood avodah zarah under it and then removed it,
chunks.st: If one erected an object of idol worship beneath a tree and subsequently removed it,

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: it is allowed.
chunks.st: it is permitted to derive benefit from the tree.

chunks.en: Which tree is an ashera?
chunks.st: Which tree is deemed forbidden as an ashera?

chunks.en: Any tree that has avodah zarah under it.
chunks.st: Any tree that has an object of idol worship beneath it.

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: any tree that people worship.
chunks.st: Any tree that people worship.

chunks.he: וּמַעֲשֶׂה בְצַיְדָּן בְּאִילָן שֶׁהָיוּ עוֹבְדִין אוֹתוֹ,
chunks.en: And there was a story in Tzaidan about a tree that people worshipped,
chunks.st: And there was an incident in Tzaidan involving a tree that people would worship,

words.note: A city.

chunks.en: and they found a pile of stones under it.
chunks.st: and Jews found beneath it a heap of stones.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon said to them,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon said to them:

chunks.en: Check this pile.
chunks.st: Examine this heap of stones.

chunks.en: They checked it and found a statue in it.
chunks.st: And they examined it and found in it an idolatrous image.

chunks.en: He said to them,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon said to them:

chunks.en: Since it is the statue they worship,
chunks.st: Since it is the image that they worship,

chunks.en: we will allow them the tree.
chunks.st: we can permit use of the tree to those who wish to derive benefit from it.

mishnayos.summary: We may not sit in the shade of an ashera tree, or walk under it. The mishnah also says when we may plant vegetables under it.

chunks.en: He should not sit in its shade,
chunks.st: With regard to an ashera, one may not sit in its shade,

chunks.en: but if he sat there, he is tahor.
chunks.st: but if one sat in its shade he remains ritually pure.

chunks.en: And he should not walk under it.
chunks.st: And one may not pass beneath it,

chunks.en: If he walked under it, he is tamei.
chunks.explain: The tree is like a roof over him.
chunks.st: and if one passed beneath it he is ritually impure.

chunks.en: If its branches stole space from the public road,
chunks.st: If the tree was robbing the public, i.e., if its branches extended over public property,

chunks.en: and he walked under it, he is tahor.
chunks.st: and one passed beneath it, he remains pure.

chunks.en: We may plant vegetables under it in the rainy season,
chunks.explain: Then its shade does not help them grow.
chunks.st: One may plant vegetables underneath an ashera during the rainy season,
chunks.stMore: as the vegetables do not benefit from its shade; on the contrary, the tree’s foliage prevents the vegetables from being properly irrigated by the rain.

chunks.en: but not in the hot season.
chunks.st: But one may not plant vegetables under an ashera during the summer,
chunks.stMore: as the shade benefits them.

chunks.he: וְהַחֲזָרִין, לֹא בִימוֹת הַחַמָּה וְלֹא בִימוֹת הַגְּשָׁמִים.
chunks.en: And lettuce — not in the hot season and not in the rainy season.
chunks.st: And lettuce may not be planted there at all, neither in the summer nor in the rainy season,
chunks.stMore: because shade is always beneficial to lettuce.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: not even vegetables in the rainy season,
chunks.st: One may not plant vegetables under an ashera even during the rainy season,

chunks.en: because the leaves fall on them
chunks.st: because the tree’s foliage [shehaneviyya] falls upon them

chunks.en: and help them grow.
chunks.st: and serves as fertilizer for them.

mishnayos.summary: Wood from an ashera tree may not be used. Bread baked with it, or cloth woven with it, is forbidden, even if it gets mixed with others. Rabbi Eliezer has a different way to fix it.

chunks.en: If he took wood from it,
chunks.st: If one took wood from an ashera,

chunks.en: we may not get any use from them.
chunks.st: it is prohibited to derive benefit from it.

chunks.en: If he heated the oven with them,
chunks.st: In a case where one kindled a fire in an oven with the wood,

chunks.en: if it is new, it must be broken.
chunks.explain: The first fire makes a new oven stronger.
chunks.st: if it is a new oven and by kindling the fire he hardened the oven and made it stronger for use in the future, then the oven must be shattered.
chunks.stMore: Since forbidden items were used in the process of forming the oven, one may not derive benefit from the use of the forbidden items.

chunks.en: If it is old, it must cool off.
chunks.st: But if it is an old oven it may be cooled;
chunks.stMore: it is prohibited to use the oven only while it is still hot.

chunks.en: If he baked bread in it,
chunks.st: If one baked bread with wood from the ashera as the fuel,

chunks.en: we may not get any use from it.
chunks.st: it is prohibited to derive benefit from the bread.

chunks.en: If it got mixed with other loaves,
chunks.st: If this bread was intermingled with other bread,

chunks.en: we may not get any use from any of them.
chunks.st: it is prohibited to derive benefit from all the bread.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: he takes the benefit to the Dead Sea.
chunks.explain: He throws away money worth the wood he used.
chunks.st: One must take the benefit and cast it into the Dead Sea.
chunks.stMore: In other words, one is not required to destroy all of the loaves. Instead, one should designate money equal in value to the wood that he used from the ashera, and he should destroy this money to offset the benefit he derived from the forbidden wood.

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: The Rabbis said to him:

chunks.en: Avodah zarah cannot be redeemed with money.
chunks.st: There is no monetary redemption for objects that are forbidden due to idol worship.
chunks.stMore: Once the bread becomes forbidden, it cannot be redeemed by having the value of the forbidden wood cast into the Dead Sea.

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: If he took a weaving tool from it,
chunks.st: If one took wood from an ashera for use as a weaving shuttle [karkor],

chunks.en: we may not get any use from it.
chunks.st: it is prohibited to derive benefit from it.

chunks.en: If he wove the cloth with it,
chunks.st: If one wove a garment with it,

chunks.en: we may not get any use from the cloth.
chunks.st: it is prohibited to derive benefit from the garment.

chunks.en: If it got mixed with others, and others with others,
chunks.st: If the garment was intermingled with other garments, and those other garments were intermingled with others,

chunks.en: we may not get any use from any of them.
chunks.st: it is prohibited to derive benefit from all of them.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: he takes the benefit to the Dead Sea.
chunks.st: One must take the benefit and cast it into the Dead Sea.

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: The Rabbis said to him:

chunks.en: Avodah zarah cannot be redeemed with money.
chunks.st: There is no monetary redemption for objects that are forbidden due to idol worship.

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

mishnayos.summary: How does a non-Jew make an ashera tree stop being an idol? If he cuts off even a leaf for his own use, it is no longer an idol.

chunks.en: How does he cancel it?
chunks.st: How does one revoke the idolatrous status of an ashera?

chunks.en: If he cut off dry branches or green twigs for himself,
chunks.st: If a gentile trimmed dry wood or pruned green wood from the tree for his own benefit,

chunks.en: or took a stick or a branch from it,
chunks.st: or if he removed from it a stick, or a rod,

chunks.en: even a leaf,
chunks.st: or even a leaf,

chunks.en: it is canceled.
chunks.explain: This shows he no longer worships it.
chunks.st: he has thereby revoked
chunks.stMore: its idolatrous status, as he has proven that he no longer worships it.

chunks.en: If he trimmed it to make it look nice, it is forbidden.
chunks.st: If a gentile shaved down the tree for its own sake, to improve its appearance, it remains prohibited to derive benefit from it.

chunks.en: If not to make it look nice, it is allowed.
chunks.st: If he shaved it down not for its own sake, it is permitted.

mishnayos.summary: Stones lying next to the idol Markulis may be forbidden, because people worshipped it by throwing stones at it. Rabbi Yishmael and the Sages argue which stones count.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yishmael says:

chunks.he: שָׁלשׁ אֲבָנִים זוֹ בְצַד זוֹ בְּצַד מַרְקוּלִיס,
chunks.en: three stones, one next to the other, next to Markulis,
chunks.st: Three stones that are adjacent to each other at the side of Mercury [Markulis]

words.note: An idol that people worshipped by throwing stones at it.

chunks.en: are forbidden.
chunks.st: are prohibited,
chunks.stMore: as that idol was worshipped by tossing stones toward it, which then became part of the idol.

chunks.en: But two are allowed.
chunks.st: But if there are only two stones, then they are permitted.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: stones that look like they are part of it are forbidden.
chunks.st: Those stones that are adjacent to Mercury and appear to have fallen from it are prohibited.

chunks.en: And ones that do not look like part of it are allowed.
chunks.st: But those stones that are not adjacent to it are permitted.

mishnayos.summary: Things found on top of an idol, like money or clothing, are allowed. But things like the ones brought on the mizbe'ach, such as wine or flour, are forbidden.

chunks.he: מָצָא בְרֹאשׁוֹ מָעוֹת, כְּסוּת אוֹ כֵלִים,
chunks.en: If he found on its head money, clothing or vessels,
chunks.st: If one found money, a garment, or vessels at the head of Mercury,

chunks.en: they are allowed.
chunks.st: these are permitted.

chunks.he: פַּרְכִּילֵי עֲנָבִים וַעֲטָרוֹת שֶׁל שִׁבֳּלִים וְיֵינוֹת
chunks.en: Bunches of grapes, crowns of grain stalks, and wine,
chunks.st: If one found vine branches laden with clusters of grapes, or wreaths made of stalks, or containers of wine,

chunks.en: and oil, and flour,
chunks.st: oil, or flour,

chunks.en: and anything like what
chunks.st: or any other item the likes of which

chunks.en: is brought on the mizbe'ach, is forbidden.
chunks.explain: It was put there as an offering to the idol.
chunks.st: is sacrificed on the altar there, it is prohibited.

mishnayos.summary: If an idol owns a garden or a bathhouse, we may use it for free, but not if we have to pay the idol's people.

chunks.he: עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁהָיָה לָהּ גִנָּה אוֹ מֶרְחָץ,
chunks.en: An avodah zarah that had a garden or a bathhouse,
chunks.st: In the case of an object of idol worship that had a garden or a bathhouse,

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: we may use them for free,
chunks.st: one may derive benefit from them when it is not to the advantage of the idol worship, i.e., when he does not pay for his use,

chunks.en: but we may not use them if we pay.
chunks.st: but one may not derive benefit from them when it is to their advantage, i.e., if one is required to pay for his use.

chunks.en: If it belonged to the idol and to other people,
chunks.st: If the garden or bathhouse belonged jointly to the place of idol worship and to others,

chunks.he: נֶהֱנִין מֵהֶן בֵּין בְּטוֹבָה וּבֵין שֶׁלֹּא בְטוֹבָה:
chunks.en: we may use them, whether we pay or not.
chunks.st: one may derive benefit from them, both when it is to their advantage and when it is not to their advantage.

mishnayos.summary: A non-Jew's idol is forbidden as soon as it is made. A non-Jew can cancel an idol so it is no longer forbidden, but a Jew cannot.

chunks.en: A non-Jew's avodah zarah
chunks.st: A gentile’s object of idol worship

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: is forbidden right away.
chunks.st: is prohibited immediately,
chunks.stMore: i.e., as soon as it is fashioned for that purpose,

chunks.en: But a Jew's
chunks.st: but a Jew’s

chunks.en: is not forbidden until it is worshipped.
chunks.st: object of idol worship is not prohibited until it is actually worshipped.

chunks.he: נָכְרִי מְבַטֵּל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁלּוֹ וְשֶׁל חֲבֵרוֹ,
chunks.en: A non-Jew can cancel the avodah zarah of himself and of his friend,
chunks.st: A gentile can revoke the status of his object of idol worship and the status of the idol of another gentile,

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.he: וְיִשְׂרָאֵל אֵינוֹ מְבַטֵּל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁל נָכְרִי.
chunks.en: but a Jew cannot cancel the avodah zarah of a non-Jew.
chunks.st: but a Jew cannot revoke the status of the object of idol worship of a gentile.

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: One who cancels the avodah zarah
chunks.st: One who revokes the status of an object of idol worship

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: has canceled its tools.
chunks.st: thereby revokes the status of its accessories.

words.note: Things used to serve the idol.

chunks.en: If he canceled its tools,
chunks.st: But if he revokes the status of its accessories,

chunks.en: the tools are allowed, but the idol is still forbidden.
chunks.st: its accessories alone are rendered permitted, but the object of idol worship itself remains prohibited.

mishnayos.summary: A non-Jew cancels an idol by breaking off a piece of it, or even by smashing it. Being angry at it for a moment does not cancel it. Rebbi and the Sages argue about selling it.

chunks.en: How does he cancel it?
If he cut off the tip of its ear,
the tip of its nose,
the tip of its finger,

chunks.he: פְּחָסָהּ אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא חִסְּרָהּ,
chunks.en: or smashed it even though no piece came off,
he canceled it.
If he spat at it,
or did something not nice in front of it,
dragged it, or threw dirt at it,
it is not canceled.
chunks.explain: He was angry for a moment, but may worship it again.

chunks.en: If he sold it or gave it as a security for a loan,
Rebbi says, he canceled it.

words.note: Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi, who wrote down the Mishnah.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
he did not cancel it.

mishnayos.summary: An idol left behind by its worshippers in peacetime is allowed, because they gave it up. In wartime it is still forbidden. Stands set up for idols when kings pass by are allowed.

chunks.he: עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁהִנִּיחוּהָ עוֹבְדֶיהָ בִּשְׁעַת שָׁלוֹם,
chunks.en: An avodah zarah that its worshippers left behind in a time of peace
chunks.st: With regard to an object of idol worship that was abandoned by its worshippers, if it was abandoned in peacetime,

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: is allowed.
chunks.explain: They left it on purpose, so they gave it up.
chunks.st: it is permitted,
chunks.stMore: as it was evidently abandoned by choice and this constitutes an implicit revocation of its status as an object of idol worship.

chunks.en: In a time of war, it is forbidden.
chunks.st: If it was abandoned in wartime, it is prohibited,
chunks.stMore: as it was not abandoned by choice.

chunks.en: The stands of kings
chunks.st: With regard to the stone platforms of kings
chunks.stMore: upon which idols are placed in honor of the kings,

chunks.en: are allowed,
chunks.st: these are permitted,

chunks.he: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמַּעֲמִידִין אוֹתָם בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁהַמְּלָכִים עוֹבְרִים:
chunks.en: because they set them up only at the time when the kings pass by.
chunks.st: due to the fact that the idol is placed on these platforms only at the time that the kings pass by.

mishnayos.summary: Non-Jews in Rome asked the Sages: if Hashem doesn't want idol worship, why doesn't He destroy the idols? The Sages explained that people also worship the sun and moon, and Hashem won't destroy His world because of fools.

chunks.en: They asked the elders in Rome,
chunks.explain: The elders are the Sages.
chunks.st: The gentiles asked the Jewish Sages who were in Rome:

chunks.en: If Hashem doesn't want avodah zarah,
chunks.st: If it is not God’s will that people should engage in idol worship,

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: why doesn't He get rid of it?
chunks.st: why does He not elimi-nate it?

chunks.en: They said to them,
chunks.st: The Sages said to them:

chunks.en: If people worshipped only things
chunks.st: Were people worshipping only objects

chunks.en: that the world does not need,
chunks.st: for which the world has no need,

chunks.en: He would get rid of them.
chunks.st: He would eliminate it.

chunks.en: But they worship the sun,
chunks.st: But they worship the sun

chunks.en: and the moon, and the stars, and the mazalos.
chunks.st: and the moon and the stars and the constellations.

words.note: Groups of stars in the sky.

chunks.en: Should He destroy His world because of the fools?
chunks.st: Should He destroy His world because of the fools?

chunks.en: They said to them,
chunks.st: The gentiles said to the Sages:

chunks.en: If so,
chunks.st: If so,

chunks.he: יְאַבֵּד דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין צֹרֶךְ לָעוֹלָם בּוֹ
chunks.en: let Him destroy the things the world does not need
chunks.st: let Him destroy those objects of idol worship for which the world has no need

chunks.en: and leave the things the world needs.
chunks.st: and leave those objects for which the world has a need.

chunks.en: They said to them,
chunks.st: The Sages said to them:

chunks.he: אַף אָנוּ מַחֲזִיקִין יְדֵי עוֹבְדֵיהֶם שֶׁל אֵלּוּ,
chunks.en: Then we would be helping the people who worship those things,
chunks.st: If that were to happen, we would thereby be supporting the worshippers of those
chunks.stMore: objects for which the world has need,

chunks.en: who would say: Know that they are gods,
chunks.st: as they would say: You should know that these are truly gods,

chunks.en: because they were not destroyed.
chunks.st: as they were not eliminated from the world, whereas the others were eliminated.

mishnayos.summary: We may buy a winepress full of trodden grapes from a non-Jew, even if he touched them. The wine becomes forbidden only once it flows down into the pit.

chunks.en: We may buy from a non-Jew a winepress where the grapes were stepped on,
chunks.st: One may purchase from a gentile a winepress in which the grapes have been trodden on,

chunks.en: even though he takes grapes
chunks.st: despite the fact that the gentile takes grapes

chunks.en: in his hand and puts them on the pile.
chunks.st: in his hand from the winepress and places them on the pile that remains to be trodden on.

chunks.en: And it does not become yayin nesech
chunks.st: And the gentile’s touch does not render the juice of the grapes wine used for a libation in idol worship, which is forbidden,

words.note: Yayin nesech is wine that might have been poured out for an idol.

chunks.en: until it flows down into the pit.
chunks.st: until it descends into the collection vat,
chunks.stMore: because until then it does not have the status of wine.

chunks.en: Once it went down into the pit,
chunks.st: Once the wine descended into the collection vat,

chunks.en: what is in the pit is forbidden,
chunks.st: that which is in the vat is prohibited,

chunks.en: and the rest is allowed.
chunks.st: and the rest, which did not yet descend into the vat, is permitted.

mishnayos.summary: We may step on grapes with a non-Jew, but not pick grapes with him. We may not help a Jew who makes his wine or bread tamei, but we may help carry things for him.

chunks.en: We may step on grapes with a non-Jew in the winepress,
chunks.st: One may tread on grapes together with the gentile in the winepress,

chunks.en: but we may not pick grapes with him.
chunks.explain: The grapes would become tamei in his winepress.
chunks.st: but one may not harvest grapes with him.
chunks.stMore: After the harvest the grapes are brought to the winepress, which is ritually impure. This would render the grapes impure, and it is prohibited to render produce of Eretz Yisrael impure.

chunks.en: A Jew who makes his wine while tamei,
chunks.st: In the case of a Jew who produces his wine in a state of ritual impurity,

chunks.en: we may not step on grapes or pick grapes with him,
chunks.st: one may not tread on grapes nor harvest them with him,
chunks.stMore: as it is prohibited to assist transgressors.

chunks.en: but we may carry barrels with him to the winepress,
chunks.st: But once he has produced his wine, one may take the barrels to the winepress with him,
chunks.stMore: as the wine is already impure.

chunks.en: and bring them with him from the winepress.
chunks.st: And one may also bring the barrels from the winepress together with him.

chunks.en: A baker who makes his bread while tamei,
chunks.st: Similarly, in the case of a baker who makes his bread in a state of ritual impurity,

chunks.en: we may not knead or shape dough with him,
chunks.st: one may not knead or arrange the dough in the shape of bread together with him,
chunks.stMore: so as not to assist in a transgression.

chunks.en: but we may carry bread with him to the bread seller.
chunks.st: But one may take the bread with him to the bread merchant [lapalter].

mishnayos.summary: When might a non-Jew have made a Jew's wine forbidden? The mishnah gives cases, like a non-Jew who fell into the wine pit or threw out a hornet with a stick.

chunks.he: גּוֹי שֶׁנִּמְצָא עוֹמֵד בְּצַד הַבּוֹר שֶׁל יַיִן,
chunks.en: A non-Jew who was found standing next to a pit of wine,
chunks.st: In the case of a gentile who was found standing next to the wine collection vat,

chunks.en: if the owner owes him money,
chunks.st: if there is a loan owed by the owner of the wine vat to the gentile,

chunks.en: it is forbidden.
chunks.explain: He thinks it is partly his, so he may touch it.
chunks.st: the wine is prohibited.
chunks.stMore: Since the gentile maintains that he has a right to the owner’s property he has no compunctions about touching the wine.

chunks.en: If the owner does not owe him money, it is allowed.
chunks.st: But if there is no loan owed by the owner of the wine vat to the gentile, the wine is permitted,
chunks.stMore: as it is assumed that the gentile did not touch the wine that was not his.

chunks.en: If he fell into the pit and came out,
chunks.st: If a gentile fell into the wine collection vat and emerged from it,

chunks.en: or measured it with a stick,
chunks.st: or if he measured the wine in the winepress with a pole
chunks.stMore: without touching it with his hands,

chunks.en: or flicked a hornet out with a stick,
chunks.st: or if he cast a hornet out of the wine by means of a pole and the pole touched the wine,

chunks.he: אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה מְטַפֵּחַ עַל פִּי חָבִית מְרֻתַּחַת,
chunks.en: or was patting down the foam on top of a bubbling barrel,
chunks.st: or where the gentile was removing the foam that was on the top of a fermenting barrel of wine;

chunks.en: all of these really happened,
chunks.st: with regard to all these cases there was such an incident.

chunks.en: and they said it should be sold.
chunks.explain: We may sell it to non-Jews, but not drink it.
chunks.st: And the Sages said that the wine may be sold to gentiles,
chunks.stMore: as it is permitted to derive benefit from the wine, but not to drink it.

chunks.en: But Rabbi Shimon allows it.
chunks.st: And Rabbi Shimon deems the wine permitted even for drinking.

chunks.he: נָטַל אֶת הֶחָבִית וּזְרָקָהּ בַּחֲמָתוֹ לַבּוֹר,
chunks.en: If he took the barrel and threw it into the pit because he was angry,
chunks.st: In a case where a gentile took the barrel of wine and threw it, in his anger, into the wine collection vat,

chunks.en: this really happened, and they said it is kosher.
chunks.st: this was an incident that occurred and the Sages deemed the wine fit for drinking.

mishnayos.summary: A Jew made a non-Jew's wine kosher and left it in the non-Jew's house. If Jews live in the city it is allowed, but in a city of only non-Jews a Jew must keep watch.

chunks.en: One who makes a non-Jew's wine kosher and puts it
chunks.st: In the case of a Jew who renders the wine of a gentile permitted by treading the gentile’s grapes so that the wine can be sold to Jews, and although a Jew has not yet paid for the wine he then places

chunks.en: in the non-Jew's home, in a house open to the public street,
chunks.st: the wine in the gentile’s domain in a house that is open to a public thoroughfare
chunks.stMore: until he sells it, the halakha depends on the circumstances.

chunks.en: in a city that has non-Jews and Jews,
chunks.st: If this occurs in a city in which there are both gentiles and Jews,

chunks.en: it is allowed.
chunks.explain: He is afraid a Jew will see him touch it.
chunks.st: the wine is permitted,
chunks.stMore: as the gentile does not touch the wine lest the Jews see him doing so.

chunks.en: In a city that is all non-Jews,
chunks.st: If this occurs in a city in which all its inhabitants are gentiles,

chunks.en: it is forbidden, unless he puts a guard there.
chunks.st: the wine is prohibited unless a Jew sits and safeguards the wine.

chunks.he: וְאֵין הַשּׁוֹמֵר צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת יוֹשֵׁב וּמְשַׁמֵּר.
chunks.en: And the guard doesn't have to sit and watch all the time.
chunks.st: But the watchman is not required to sit and guard the wine constantly;

chunks.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא יוֹצֵא וְנִכְנָס,
chunks.en: Even if he goes out and comes in,
chunks.st: even if he frequently leaves the place and comes in again later,

chunks.en: it is allowed.
chunks.st: the wine is permitted.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:

chunks.en: all places of non-Jews are the same.
chunks.st: The domain of gentiles is all one,
chunks.stMore: as the Gemara will explain.

mishnayos.summary: A Jew made a non-Jew's wine kosher and left it with him. If the non-Jew wrote that he was paid, it is allowed. If he won't let the Jew take it until he pays, it is forbidden.

chunks.he: הַמְּטַהֵר יֵינוֹ שֶׁל נָכְרִי וְנוֹתְנוֹ בִרְשׁוּתוֹ,
chunks.en: One who makes a non-Jew's wine kosher and puts it in his home,
chunks.st: In the case of a Jew who renders the wine of a gentile permitted by treading the gentile’s grapes so that the wine can be sold to Jews, and he then places the wine in the gentile’s domain
chunks.stMore: until he sells it, the halakha depends on the circumstances.

chunks.en: and the non-Jew writes to him,
chunks.st: If that one, the gentile, writes for the Jew:

chunks.en: "I got money from you,"
chunks.st: I received money from you
chunks.stMore: in payment for the wine, even though he did not yet receive the actual payment,

chunks.en: it is allowed.
chunks.explain: The wine is the Jew's, so he won't touch it.
chunks.st: the wine is permitted.
chunks.stMore: This is because the wine is considered the Jew’s property and the gentile does not venture to touch it.

chunks.en: But if the Jew wants to take it out,
chunks.st: But if the Jew desires to remove the wine

chunks.he: וְאֵינוֹ מַנִּיחוֹ עַד שֶׁיִּתֵּן לוֹ אֶת מְעוֹתָיו,
chunks.en: and the non-Jew won't let him until he gives him his money,
chunks.st: and the gentile does not allow him to do so until the Jew gives him the money due to him,

chunks.en: this really happened in Beis She'an,
chunks.st: this was an incident that occurred in Beit She’an

chunks.en: and the Sages forbade it.
chunks.st: and the Sages deemed the wine prohibited.
chunks.stMore: In this case the gentile believes that he has a lien upon the wine, and therefore he has no compunctions about touching it.

mishnayos.summary: If a non-Jew pays a Jew to work with yayin nesech, the Jew may not use the pay. But if he was hired for other work, the pay is allowed.

chunks.he: הַשּׂוֹכֵר אֶת הַפּוֹעֵל לַעֲשׂוֹת עִמּוֹ בְיֵין נֶסֶךְ,
chunks.en: One who hires a worker to work with him with yayin nesech,
chunks.st: In the case of a gentile who hires a Jewish laborer to work with wine used for an idolatrous libation with him,

words.note: Yayin nesech is wine that might have been poured out for an idol.

chunks.en: his pay is forbidden.
chunks.st: his wage is forbidden,
chunks.stMore: i.e., it is prohibited for the Jew to derive benefit from his wage.

chunks.en: If he hired him to do other work with him,
chunks.st: If the gentile hired him to do other work with him,

chunks.en: even if he said to him,
chunks.st: even if he said to him while he was working with him:

chunks.en: "Move for me a barrel
chunks.st: Transport the barrel

chunks.en: of yayin nesech from place to place,"
chunks.st: of wine used for a libation for me from this place to that place,

chunks.en: his pay is allowed.
chunks.st: his wage is permitted,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the Jew is permitted to derive benefit from the money.

chunks.he: הַשׂוֹכֵר אֶת הַחֲמוֹר לְהָבִיא עָלֶיהָ יֵין נֶסֶךְ,
chunks.en: One who rents a Jew's donkey to carry yayin nesech on it,
chunks.st: With regard to a gentile who rents a Jew’s donkey to carry wine used for a libation on it,

words.note: Yayin nesech is wine that might have been poured out for an idol.

chunks.en: its rent money is forbidden.
chunks.st: its rental fee is forbidden.

chunks.en: If he rented it to sit on it,
chunks.st: If he rented it to sit on it,

chunks.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהִנִּיחַ הַגּוֹי לְגִינוֹ עָלֶיהָ,
chunks.en: even though the non-Jew put his jug of wine on it,
chunks.st: even if a gentile placed his jug of wine used for a libation on it,

chunks.en: its rent money is allowed.
chunks.st: its rental fee is permitted.

mishnayos.summary: If yayin nesech falls on fruit, the fruit is forbidden only if the wine's taste makes it better. A taste that spoils the food does not make it forbidden.

chunks.he: יֵין נֶסֶךְ שֶׁנָּפַל עַל גַּבֵּי עֲנָבִים,
chunks.en: Yayin nesech that fell on grapes,
chunks.st: In the case of wine used for a libation that fell on grapes,

words.note: Yayin nesech is wine that might have been poured out for an idol.

chunks.en: he washes them and they are allowed.
chunks.st: one rinses them and they are permitted.

chunks.en: But if they were split open, they are forbidden.
chunks.st: But if the grapes were cracked, they are forbidden.

chunks.en: If it fell on figs
chunks.st: In a case where the wine fell on figs

chunks.en: or on dates,
chunks.st: or on dates,

chunks.he: אִם יֵשׁ בָּהֶן בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם, אָסוּר.
chunks.en: if there is enough to give them a taste, they are forbidden.
chunks.st: if there is sufficient wine in them to impart flavor, they are forbidden.

chunks.en: There was a story with Baisos ben Zonen,
chunks.st: And there was an incident involving Boethus ben Zunen,

chunks.en: who brought dried figs in a ship,
chunks.st: who transported dried figs in a ship,

chunks.en: and a barrel of yayin nesech broke
chunks.st: and a barrel of wine used for a libation broke

chunks.en: and fell on them,
chunks.st: and fell on them,

chunks.en: and he asked the Sages and they allowed them.
chunks.st: and he asked the Sages as to the halakha, and the Sages deemed the figs permitted.

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: This is the principle:

chunks.en: anything where the taste helps it, is forbidden.
chunks.st: Anything that benefits from a forbidden item imparting flavor to it, i.e., the forbidden item contributes a positive taste to it, is forbidden,

chunks.he: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין בַּהֲנָאָתוֹ בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם, מֻתָּר,
chunks.en: Anything where the taste does not help it, is allowed,
chunks.st: and anything that does not benefit from a forbidden item imparting flavor to it is permitted,

chunks.he: כְּגוֹן חֹמֶץ שֶׁנָּפַל עַל גַּבֵּי גְרִיסִין:
chunks.en: like vinegar that fell on split beans.
chunks.explain: The vinegar does not make the beans taste better.
chunks.st: such as forbidden vinegar that fell onto split beans,
chunks.stMore: as the flavor imparted by the vinegar does not enhance the taste of the beans.

mishnayos.summary: A non-Jew was carrying wine together with a Jew. If the non-Jew thinks the Jew is watching, the wine is allowed. If the Jew said he was going far away, it depends on how long he was gone.

chunks.en: A non-Jew who was moving, together with a Jew,
chunks.st: With regard to a gentile who was transporting

chunks.en: jugs of wine from place to place,
chunks.st: barrels of wine from one place to another place together with a Jew,

chunks.en: if it was as if it was being watched, it is allowed.
chunks.st: if the wine was under the presumption of being supervised, it is permitted.

chunks.en: If he told him that he was going far away,
chunks.st: But if the Jew notified him that he was going far away,

chunks.en: it is forbidden if he was gone long enough to make a hole, close it, and let it dry.
chunks.st: the wine is forbidden if the Jew left for a sufficient amount of time for the gentile to bore a hole [sheyishtom] in the barrel, seal it again with plaster, and for the plaster to dry.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: only if he was gone long enough to open it, plug it again, and let it dry.
chunks.st: The wine is forbidden only if it was sufficient time for the gentile to open the barrel by removing the stopper altogether, stop it again by making a new stopper, and for the new stopper to dry.

mishnayos.summary: A Jew who leaves his wine with a non-Jew, or leaves a non-Jew in his store, has to worry only if he said he would be gone for a long time.

chunks.en: One who left his wine in a wagon or in a ship,
chunks.st: With regard to one who placed his wine in a wagon or on a ship

chunks.en: and went off by a shortcut,
chunks.explain: The non-Jew doesn't know when he will come back.
chunks.st: with a gentile, and went on his way by a shortcut [bekappendarya],
chunks.stMore: such that the gentile does not know when the Jew will encounter him,

chunks.en: even if he went into the city and bathed,
chunks.st: even if the Jew entered the city and bathed,

chunks.en: it is allowed.
chunks.st: the wine is permitted,
chunks.stMore: because the gentile would not use the wine for a libation, for fear the owner might catch him at it.

chunks.en: If he told him that he was going far away,
chunks.st: If the Jew informed the gentile that he was going away for a long period of time,

chunks.en: it is forbidden if he was gone long enough to make a hole, close it, and let it dry.
chunks.st: the wine is forbidden if it was sufficient time for the gentile to bore a hole in the barrel, seal it again with plaster, and for the plaster to dry.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: only if he was gone long enough to open it, plug it again, and let it dry.
chunks.st: It is forbidden only if it was sufficient time for him to open the barrel by removing the stopper altogether, stop it again, and for the new stopper to dry.

chunks.en: One who leaves a non-Jew in his store,
chunks.st: With regard to one who left a gentile in his shop,

chunks.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא יוֹצֵא וְנִכְנָס,
chunks.en: even if he goes out and comes in,
chunks.st: even if the Jew went out and came in and was not there all the time,

chunks.en: it is allowed.
chunks.st: the wine is permitted.

chunks.en: But if he told him that he was going far away,
chunks.st: But if the Jew informed the gentile that he was going away for a long period of time,

chunks.en: it is forbidden if he was gone long enough to make a hole, close it, and let it dry.
chunks.st: the wine is forbidden if it was sufficient time for the gentile to bore a hole in the barrel, seal it again with plaster, and for the plaster to dry.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: only if he was gone long enough to open it, plug it again, and let it dry.
chunks.st: The wine is forbidden only if it was sufficient time for him to open the barrel, stop it again, and for the new stopper to dry.

mishnayos.summary: A Jew ate with a non-Jew and stepped out. The wine on the table is forbidden, but the wine on the side table is allowed, unless he told the non-Jew to help himself.

chunks.en: If he was eating with him at the table,
chunks.st: If a Jew was eating with a gentile at the table,

chunks.en: and left a jug of wine on the table,
chunks.st: and left jugs [laginin] of wine on the table

chunks.en: and a jug on the side table,
chunks.st: and a jug on the side table [hadulebaki],

chunks.en: and left him and went out,
chunks.st: and he left it and went out,

chunks.en: what is on the table is forbidden.
chunks.st: what is on the table is forbidden,
chunks.stMore: as it is likely that the gentile handled it,

chunks.en: And what is on the side table is allowed.
chunks.st: whereas what is on the side table is permitted.

chunks.he: וְאִם אָמַר לוֹ הֱוֵי מוֹזֵג וְשׁוֹתֶה,
chunks.en: But if he said to him, "Pour and drink,"
chunks.st: But if the Jew said to the gentile: Mix water with the wine and drink,

chunks.en: even what is on the side table is forbidden.
chunks.st: even the jug that is on the side table is forbidden.

chunks.en: Open barrels are forbidden.
chunks.st: Similarly, open barrels are forbidden,

chunks.en: Closed ones are allowed,
chunks.st: but sealed barrels are permitted

chunks.en: unless he was gone long enough to open one, plug it again, and let it dry.
chunks.st: unless the Jew was out of the room for sufficient time for the gentile to open the barrel by removing the stopper, and stop it again by making a new stopper, and for the new stopper to dry.

mishnayos.summary: If soldiers came into a city in peacetime, open barrels of wine are forbidden afterwards. In wartime, all the barrels are allowed, because there is no time to pour wine for idols.

chunks.he: בַּלֶּשֶׁת גּוֹיִם שֶׁנִּכְנְסָה לָעִיר בִּשְׁעַת שָׁלוֹם,
chunks.en: A troop of non-Jewish soldiers that came into a city in a time of peace,
chunks.st: In the case of a military unit [boleshet] that entered a city, if it entered during peacetime,

chunks.en: open barrels are forbidden.
chunks.st: then after the soldiers leave the open barrels of wine are forbidden,

chunks.en: Closed ones are allowed.
chunks.st: but the sealed barrels are permitted.

chunks.en: In a time of war,
chunks.st: If the unit entered in wartime,

chunks.en: all of them are allowed,
chunks.st: both these barrels and those barrels are permitted,

chunks.en: because there is no time to pour wine for idols.
chunks.st: because in wartime there is no time to pour wine for libations, and one can be certain that the soldiers did not do so.

mishnayos.summary: Jewish workers who are paid with yayin nesech may ask for money instead, before it reaches them. The mishnah also teaches how selling and pouring wine for a non-Jew can make it forbidden.

chunks.he: אֻמָּנִין שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁשָּׁלַח לָהֶם נָכְרִי
chunks.en: Jewish craftsmen to whom a non-Jew sent
chunks.st: With regard to Jewish craftsmen to whom a gentile sent

chunks.en: a barrel of yayin nesech as their pay,
chunks.st: a barrel of wine used for a libation in lieu of their wage,

chunks.he: מֻתָּרִים לוֹמַר לוֹ תֵּן לָנוּ אֶת דָּמֶיהָ.
chunks.en: are allowed to say to him: "Give us its value in money."
chunks.st: it is permitted for them to say to him: Give us its monetary value instead.

chunks.en: But once it came into their hands, it is forbidden.
chunks.st: But once it has entered into their possession, it is prohibited for them to say so,
chunks.stMore: as that would be tantamount to selling the wine to the gentile and deriving benefit from it.

chunks.en: One who sells his wine to a non-Jew,
chunks.st: In the case of a Jew who sells his wine to a gentile,

chunks.en: if he set the price before he measured it out,
chunks.st: if he fixed a price before he measured the wine into the gentile’s vessel,

chunks.en: its money is allowed.
chunks.explain: The non-Jew made the wine forbidden only after buying it.
chunks.st: deriving benefit from the money paid for the wine is permitted.
chunks.stMore: It is not tantamount to selling wine used for a libation, as the gentile purchased the wine before it became forbidden, and the money already belonged to the Jew.

chunks.en: If he measured it out before he set the price,
chunks.st: But if the Jew measured the wine into the gentile’s vessel, thereby rendering it forbidden, before he fixed a price,

chunks.en: its money is forbidden.
chunks.st: the money paid for the wine is forbidden.

chunks.en: If he took the funnel and measured wine
chunks.st: In a case where a Jew took a funnel and measured

chunks.en: into the non-Jew's bottle,
chunks.st: wine into a gentile’s jug,

chunks.he: וְחָזַר וּמָדַד לְתוֹךְ צְלוֹחִיתוֹ שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
chunks.en: and then measured into a Jew's bottle,
chunks.st: and then measured wine with the same funnel into a Jew’s jug,

chunks.he: אִם יֶשׁ בּוֹ עַכֶּבֶת יַיִן, אָסוּר.
chunks.en: if there is some wine left in the funnel, it is forbidden.
chunks.st: if there is a remnant of wine left in the funnel, the wine measured into the Jew’s jug is forbidden,
chunks.stMore: as some of the wine that was measured into the gentile’s jug is mixed in it.

chunks.en: One who pours from one vessel to another,
chunks.st: In the case of one who pours wine from one vessel into another vessel,

chunks.en: what is left in the one he poured from is allowed,
chunks.st: the wine left in the vessel from which he poured is permitted,

chunks.en: but what he poured into is forbidden.
chunks.st: but the wine in the vessel into which he poured is forbidden.

mishnayos.summary: Yayin nesech makes even a big amount of wine forbidden if it gets mixed in. If it mixes with something different, like water, it makes it forbidden only if you can taste it.

chunks.en: Yayin nesech is forbidden,
chunks.st: Wine used for a libation is forbidden,

words.note: Yayin nesech is wine that might have been poured out for an idol.

chunks.en: and it makes other wine forbidden with any amount.
chunks.st: and any amount of it renders other wine forbidden if they are mixed together.

chunks.en: Wine in wine, and water in water,
chunks.st: Wine used for a libation that became mixed with wine, or water that was used for an idolatrous libation that became mixed with ordinary water,

chunks.en: with any amount.
chunks.st: renders the mixture forbidden with any amount of the forbidden wine or water;

chunks.en: Wine in water, and water in wine,
chunks.st: but wine used for a libation that became mixed with water, or water used for a libation that became mixed with wine

chunks.en: only if it gives a taste.
chunks.st: renders the mixture forbidden only if the forbidden liquid is sufficient to impart flavor to the mixture, i.e., for the wine to flavor the water or for the water to dilute the wine to an extent that can be tasted.

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: This is the principle:

chunks.en: the same kind mixed with its own kind, with any tiny amount.
chunks.st: A substance in contact with the same type of substance renders the mixture forbidden with any amount of the forbidden substance,

chunks.en: But with a different kind, only if it gives a taste.
chunks.st: but a substance in contact with a different type of substance renders the mixture forbidden only in a case where it imparts flavor to it.

mishnayos.summary: Some forbidden things are so strict that even a tiny bit mixed into a lot makes it all forbidden. The mishnah lists them.

chunks.en: These are forbidden,
chunks.st: These following items are themselves forbidden,

chunks.en: and they make others forbidden with any amount:
chunks.st: and any amount of them renders other items with which they become mixed forbidden:

chunks.en: yayin nesech,
chunks.st: Wine used for a libation;

chunks.en: and avodah zarah,
chunks.st: and objects of idol worship;

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: and animal skins cut open at the heart,
chunks.st: and hides with a tear opposite the heart,
chunks.stMore: indicating the idolatrous practice of sacrificing hearts of live animals.

chunks.en: and an ox that is to be stoned,
chunks.st: And this halakha also applies to an ox that has been condemned to be stoned (see Exodus 21:28),
chunks.stMore: from which it is prohibited to derive benefit even before its sentence is carried out;

words.note: An ox that killed a person is put to death by stoning.

chunks.en: and an eglah arufah,
chunks.st: and it applies to a heifer whose neck is broken
chunks.stMore: when a person is found killed in an area between two cities and the murderer is unknown (see Deuteronomy 21:1–9), which is likewise forbidden from the time it is taken down to the river to be killed. In these cases, if the animal becomes mixed in a herd of similar animals, all of the animals in the herd are forbidden.

words.note: The eglah arufah, brought when a person is found dead and no one knows who killed him.

chunks.en: and the birds of a metzora,
chunks.st: And this halakha also applies to birds designated for the purification of a leper (Leviticus 14:1–6),

words.note: A person with tzaraas, a skin sickness from the Torah.

chunks.en: and the hair of a nazir,
chunks.st: and the shorn hair of a nazirite (Numbers 6:18),

words.note: A person who promised not to drink wine or cut his hair.

chunks.en: and a firstborn donkey,
chunks.st: and a firstborn donkey (Exodus 13:13),

chunks.en: and meat cooked in milk,
chunks.st: and meat that was cooked in milk (Exodus 23:19),

chunks.en: and the goat sent away on Yom Kippur,
chunks.st: and the scape-goat of Yom Kippur (Leviticus 16:7–10),

chunks.en: and chulin animals slaughtered in the Beis HaMikdash courtyard,
chunks.st: and the meat of a non-sacred animal that was slaughtered in the Temple courtyard.

words.note: Food that is not holy.

chunks.he: הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ אֲסוּרִין וְאוֹסְרִין בְּכָל שֶׁהֵן:
chunks.en: all these are forbidden and make others forbidden with any amount.
chunks.st: All of these are forbidden themselves, and any amount of them renders a mixture forbidden.

mishnayos.summary: If yayin nesech falls into a pit of wine, all the wine becomes forbidden. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says it may be sold to a non-Jew, except for the value of the forbidden wine.

chunks.en: Yayin nesech that fell into a pit of wine,
chunks.st: In the case of wine used for a libation that fell into a wine cistern,

words.note: Yayin nesech is wine that might have been poured out for an idol.

chunks.en: all of it is forbidden for any use.
chunks.st: it is prohibited to derive benefit from all of the wine in the cistern,
chunks.stMore: even if the volume of the wine used for a libation was tiny in comparison to the volume of the wine in the cistern.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: all of it may be sold to a non-Jew,
chunks.st: All of the wine in the cistern may be sold to a gentile,

chunks.en: except for the value of the yayin nesech in it.
chunks.st: and the money paid for it is permitted except for the value of the wine used for a libation that is included in it.

mishnayos.summary: How do we make a winepress kosher after a non-Jew coated it with tar? It depends on whether it is made of stone, wood or clay.

chunks.en: A stone winepress that a non-Jew coated with tar,
chunks.st: In the case of a stone winepress that a gentile lined with pitch
chunks.stMore: and then poured wine onto the pitch to neutralize its flavor,

words.en: that he coated it with tar

chunks.en: he wipes it and it is kosher.
chunks.st: one may cleanse it and it is pure,
chunks.stMore: i.e., wine pressed in it is permitted.

chunks.en: And a wooden one,
chunks.st: And if the winepress is fashioned of wood,

chunks.en: Rebbi says, he wipes it.
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says: One may cleanse it,

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: but the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: he must peel off the tar.
chunks.st: One must peel off the pitch completely.

chunks.en: And a clay one,
chunks.st: And if the winepress is of earthenware,

chunks.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁקָּלַף אֶת הַזֶּפֶת,
chunks.en: even if he peeled off the tar,
chunks.st: even if one peeled off the pitch,

chunks.en: it is forbidden.
chunks.st: this press is forbidden.

mishnayos.summary: Pots and tools bought from a non-Jew must be made kosher in the way they were used: dipping in a mikveh, boiling water, or fire. A knife is polished.

chunks.en: One who buys kitchen tools from a non-Jew,
chunks.st: One who purchases cooking utensils from the gentiles
chunks.stMore: must prepare them for use by Jews in the following manner:

chunks.en: one that is usually only dipped in a mikveh,
chunks.st: With regard to those utensils whose manner of preparation is to immerse them in a ritual bath,
chunks.stMore: as they require no further preparation,

chunks.en: he dips it.
chunks.st: he must immerse them accordingly.

chunks.en: One that needs boiling water,
chunks.st: With regard to those utensils whose manner of preparation is to purge them with boiling water,
chunks.stMore: as those utensils are used with boiling water, e.g., pots,

chunks.en: he puts it in boiling water.
chunks.st: he must purge them accordingly.

words.en: he should kasher it in boiling water.

chunks.en: One that needs to be made red-hot in fire,
chunks.st: With regard to those whose manner of preparation is to heat until white-hot in the fire,
chunks.stMore: as they are used for grilling,

chunks.en: he makes it red-hot in fire.
chunks.st: he must heat them until white-hot in the fire.

chunks.en: The roasting spit and the grill,
chunks.st: Therefore, with regard to the spit [hashappud] and the grill [veha’askela],

chunks.en: he makes them red-hot in fire.
chunks.st: he must heat them until white-hot in the fire.

chunks.en: The knife, he polishes it and it is kosher.
chunks.st: With regard to the knife, he must polish it and it is rendered pure.
